english.title: Use / cause / permit use of vehicle without recording equipment
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY THE OFFENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 97ZA(1)(a) and (2) of the Transport Act 1968.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
used / caused / permitted the use of
a passenger / goods vehicle OR
a vehicle within Article 4 of the Community Drivers' Hours Regulation that was not referred to in Article 3
without vehicle recording equipment which
was installed in accordance with the AETR AND
complied with the AETR including and the Annex to the AETR AND
was being used as provided by Article 10 to 13 of the Annex to the AETR

english.notes:
(i) The graduated fixed penalty system applies to this offence; therefore the fixed penalty that can be issued will vary, dependant on the severity of the offence in each case. For details of which fixed penalty amount applies to a particular offence, see paragraph 3A of Schedule 2 to the Fixed Penalty Order 2000.
(ii) Section 97ZA(3) provides that the offence will not be made out where a person proves to the court that the person knew nor ought to have known that the recording equipment had not been installed in line with the AETR.
(iii) Section 97ZA(4) provides that a person will not be liable under subsection (1)(a) if the person proves to the court that the vehicle in question was proceeding to a place where recording equipment which would comply with the AETR was to be installed in the vehicle in accordance with the AETR.
(iv) Section 97ZA(5) provides that a person will not be liable under subsection (1)(a) if the person proves to the court that the recording equipment was not in working order as it had not become reasonably practical for the equipment to be repaired by an approved fitter/workshop or, the requirements of Article 13(2)(a) of the Annex to the AETR were being complied with.
(v) Section 97ZA(6) provides a person will not be liable under subsection (1)(a) where a seal of recording equipment has been broken if it can be proved that the breaking / removal of the seal could not be avoided; it had not been reasonably practical for the seal to be replaced by an approved fitter or workshop; and in all other respects the equipment was being used as provided by Articles 10 to 13 of the Annex to the AETR.
(vi) Section 97ZA(7) states that a person will not be liable for contravening subsection (1)(a) by reason of a driver card not being used with recording equipment installed in the vehicle if the driver card was damaged, malfunctioning, lost or stolen; the requirements of Articles 12(1), 13(2) and (3) of the Annex to the AETR were being complied with; and in all other aspects the recording equipment was being used as provided by Articles 10 to 13 of the Annex to the AETR.
(vii) Section 97ZA(8) provides that individuals using vehicles in the course of employment will be personally liable if they act in contravention of section 97ZA(1) however their employer also commits an offence where the section has been made out.
